tagline.text: A pilgrimage church in the Cagayan Valley housing the brown Our Lady of Piat

location.label: Location
location.text: Poblacion, Piat, Cagayan, northwest of Tuguegarao City

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: December–May dry season; pilgrimage season is late June to early July

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱300–1,500 (per person, round-trip transport from Tuguegarao and snacks)

children.text: Piat Basilica is a red-brick church on a hill in Piat, Cagayan, home to the brown image of Our Lady of Piat, venerated for more than 400 years. It is about 30 minutes by road from Tuguegarao, so you can combine a Cagayan Valley pilgrimage and church tour in a single trip.

Piat Basilica is a Roman Catholic church standing on a low hill in the Poblacion of Piat, in southwestern Cagayan. Its official name is the Basilica Minore of Our Lady of Piat, and it belongs to the Archdiocese of Tuguegarao. It lies about
41km
northwest of Tuguegarao City, usually
30 minutes
or so by road, and about
507km
from Manila overland. This area is home to the Itawes people, so you can feel a distinctive atmosphere in the Cagayan Valley where Ibanag, Itawes and Ilocano are all spoken.

The main reason the church is famous is the image it houses. According to records, the image came from Macau, reached Manila in 1604 and was brought to the Cagayan region, where Dominican friars first called it Our Lady of the Most Holy Rosary. Because of its dark complexion it is known as the Black Madonna or Brown Madonna, and locally it is called the Mother of Cagayan. The image passed through Lal-lo (the former Nueva Segovia), Tuguegarao and other places, and in 1622 it is said to have returned to Piat at the urging of the townspeople. On December 26, 1623, a procession carried it to its new sanctuary, and the Mass the following day is recorded as drawing more than 10,000 people.

The present church is a red-brick building in a Romanesque style, and it is said to have been restored by Fr. José Gurumeta in 1875. It was built on a hill about one mile from the town's parish church, away from the flooding of the Chico River. The exterior has a plain facade with a tall belfry on the left, and the interior has a curved wooden ceiling and gallery-like verandas. The image is enshrined behind glass behind the altar. On March 10, 1997, a decree of Pope John Paul II gave the church the status of Minor Basilica, and as one of the few basilicas in the Philippines it is called the Pilgrimage Center of Northeast Luzon.

This guide is for travelers staying in Tuguegarao or elsewhere in the Cagayan Valley who want to visit Piat on a half-day trip. On weekdays without religious events you can explore the building and the hill in peace, while the Sambali Festival in late June and the feast of Our Lady on July 1–2 bring crowds of pilgrims. Even if you are not a believer, it is worth visiting for the church architecture, the pilgrimage culture and the local snacks. Mass times and events can change from year to year, so check with the archdiocese or the parish before you go.

A brown image of the Virgin enshrined behind glass behind the altar. If you climb the stairs at the back of the church, a small window directly behind the image lets you touch the hem of Mary's dress and pray. On days with many pilgrims the line gets long, so wait your turn quietly.

A simple building made of the red brick commonly used for churches in the Cagayan Valley. Notice the left belfry, the curved wooden ceiling, and the historical paintings and explanations on the upper walls. The entrance arch is inscribed with a line of the Hail Mary in the local language.

The entrance arch of this church is at the back of the building, so the side you see from the front is not the side you enter from. On a first visit you have to walk around the building, so check the way at the foot of the hill before you climb.
The museum next to the church displays artifacts and materials related to the church and to devotion to Our Lady of Piat. Opening hours may change often, so it is safest to confirm on arrival.

blocks.title: Rosary garden and Stations of the Cross

children.text: Around the church there are life-size Stations of the Cross sculptures, a rosary garden with statues of the Twelve Apostles, a baptistry and a place to light votive candles. It is a short, pleasant walk that you can take slowly before or after Mass.

blocks.title: Sambali Festival and feast of Our Lady

children.text: Every year from
June 23–30
the Sambali Festival, named after an old tribal war dance called sambali, is held with novenas, street dancing and cultural performances. The feast of Our Lady is on
July 1–2
. Dates can vary from year to year, so check the latest announcements.

blocks.title: The healing spring Bukal ng Buhay

children.text: Near the church hill there is a spring called Bukal ng Buhay (Spring of Life) that pilgrims have visited since April 2005. Some people drink or take the water hoping for healing, but understand it as an act of faith and use your own judgment about hygiene.

Along the road outside the church there are stalls selling religious items, tobacco and snacks such as rice cakes. Pawa, a sticky rice cake filled with sweetened ground peanuts, is a local specialty worth trying while it is warm.
From your hotel in Tuguegarao, go to the west terminal or minibus stop and take a van to Piat.
Arrive in Piat, walk from the foot of the hill to the rear entrance of the church, and look around the nave and altar.
Climb the back stairs to the window behind the image to pray, then walk slowly through the museum and the rosary garden.
Try a snack such as pawa at the stalls in front of the church and browse the souvenirs.
Have lunch in town and head back toward Tuguegarao.
Traffic is heavy on Sundays and feast days because of Mass crowds, so allow extra travel time. Travel is much easier on weekdays.
Have breakfast near Tuguegarao Cathedral and see an early Mass or the exterior first.
Go to Piat by van or rental car. On a weekday it takes about
30 minutes–1 hour
Look around Piat Basilica, including the window behind the image and the museum.
After lunch, on the way back to Tuguegarao, continue to Iguig Calvary Hills if time allows.
When combining several churches, it is easier to rent a car for the day. Agree on the fare with the driver first.
The domestic flight from Ninoy Aquino International Airport in Manila to Tuguegarao Airport (TUG) takes about
1 hour
. Airlines and schedules change by season, so check when you book.
From the airport, take a taxi or tricycle into Tuguegarao, then travel on to Piat from the city.
Because this is a route with few flights, it is safer to book early in peak season.
From Manila, take a Tuguegarao coach at a terminal such as Cubao. Allow about
10–12 hours
and check the departure terminal when booking.
After arriving in Tuguegarao, transfer to a van or rental car for Piat. The last van leaves early, so check locally.
Piat is about
41 km
from central Tuguegarao. In a 2026 public transport example, Piat Junction took about
1 hour
to reach, followed by a tricycle to the basilica.

for a tricycle from Piat Junction to the basilica. Ask locally where the return service terminates.
For a comfortable day trip, you can rent a vehicle for the day through your hotel or a local driver and visit Iguig and Piat together.
You can explore the town of Piat and the area around the church on foot. For longer distances use a tricycle and ask the fare before you get in.

The Cagayan Valley is very hot and humid in the middle of the day. For a relaxed walk around the church, December–February is the most comfortable, being cooler and drier, while March–May is very hot, so start early.

If you want to feel the pilgrimage atmosphere, you can go during the Sambali Festival (late June) and the feast of Our Lady (July 1–2). However, expect crowds and traffic jams and difficulty finding rooms, so prepare early.

Piat is a small town with few places to stay. Some reports mention a small inn near the church, but it can be hard to find, so most visitors stay in central Tuguegarao and come for the day. During festivals all rooms fill up early, so book in advance. Hotel names and rates change over time, so check recent reviews on booking sites.

Food centers on local snacks. Pawa, a rice cake filled with sweetened ground peanuts, is sold in front of the church and tastes best warm. For lunch, eat in town or return to Tuguegarao for pancit batil patong (a Tuguegarao specialty of noodles topped with an egg). Choose street food only after checking its hygiene with your own eyes.
The church is a place of worship, so dress with shoulders and knees covered and avoid taking photos during Mass.
The entrance is at the back of the building, so if you cannot find the door at the front, walk around the building.
On Sundays and feast days the Mass crowds are large, so arrive early if you want a seat.
Bring a hat, sunscreen and water. You spend a lot of time climbing the hill and walking outdoors, and midday is very hot.
When praying at the window behind the image, do not stay long, out of consideration for the people behind you.
Opening hours of facilities such as the museum and the spring are not fixed, so confirm on site.
Carry enough cash. ATMs can be scarce in town.
If you plan a Cagayan Valley church tour, it is efficient to combine Tuguegarao Cathedral and Iguig.
During the feast of Our Lady of Piat and the Sambali Festival there are traffic controls and extreme congestion, so secure your travel time and accommodation in advance.
Exact Mass times and event schedules change every year. Check the latest announcements from the archdiocese or parish.
On days with many pilgrims pickpockets may be about, so keep valuables in front of your body.
The transport fares in this guide are based partly on older reports and may differ from current ones.
Use the spring water and street food at your own discretion regarding hygiene, and avoid them if you feel unwell.
During typhoon and heavy-rain periods, roads around the Chico River may be in poor condition, so check weather and road information.
The center of Cagayan, where you can enjoy the cathedral, the Chapel of San Jacinto and local food such as pancit batil patong. It is about
30–45 minutes
from Piat by car.
A limestone cave in Peñablanca near Tuguegarao; set aside a separate day for it if you want to add a nature outing to your church tour.
Iguig, close to Tuguegarao, has Stations of the Cross sculptures and a red-brick church, making it a good pilgrimage stop to combine with Piat on the same day.
Lal-lo, the former Nueva Segovia where the image of Our Lady of Piat was once kept, lies on the lower Cagayan River and suits a history trip. It is far away, so plan it as a separate outing.
